main_text.p: meritatoleraremus, non digni essemus, &c. Quar-tò, Remigius.{P}Etsi omnia praecepta utriusque Testamenti quis praestiterit, tamen non est dignus illa gloriâ. (supra, cap. 14.)

Ratio quarta argumentandi cernitur in his Patrum phrasibus, viz. Primò, monendo ut Martyres confiderent se non plus pati, quàm pro peccatis merebantur. Sic Hieronymus. Et iisdem prorsus verbis Primasius. Quibuscum Isidorus Hispalensis consentit. Denique, Dicitur ab Apostolo, NON SUNT CONDIGNÆ PASSIONES HUJUS TEM-PORIS &c. ad deprimendam Patientium superbiam. Hæc singula pleniùs exprimuntur su-prà [?], cap. 14.

p.i: Antiquorum Patrum testimonia insuper alia, quæ probant Martyrium ipsum non esse opus Meritorium Condignum vitâ æternâ, ex Psal. 116.

main_text.head: SECT. III.
main_text.p: PSalm. 116. (secundùm vulgatam, 115) Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ accepi? Calicem Salutis accipiam, & nomen Domini invocabo. —Pretiosa mors Sanctorum in conspectu ejus. Non hîc contendimus de genuino & literali hujus textûs sensu, sed de antiquorum Patrum judiciis (quod ad Martyrium spectat) quæ scriptis suis confignârunt.

page.notes: Printed "Sect. 3." in the running head is read as "3". The word "meritatoleraremus" at the start of the continued paragraph is partly worn. The hyphenated "su-prà" at the end of the paragraph is read with doubt, since the first letter could be "f". The large initials "A" (Antiquorum) and "P" (PSalm.) are decorative and joined to the following word. The marginal note "P Remigius." is set in the right margin. Show-through from the facing page on the right margin has been left out.
